# Design contract: Multi-cloud architecture editor (proposal v0)

## 1. Product decision (one sentence)
Adopt a hybrid model: one authoritative provider-neutral resource registry and inventory, plus intent-based diagram projections that reference resource records and render them through a deterministic semantic presentation taxonomy, so the default diagram stays truthful and readable while every resource remains discoverable, inspectable, editable as authorized, and exportable.

## 2. Conceptual model (three planes)
- Resource plane (truth): Resource Record = identity (provider, type, external ID) + versioned type metadata reference + instance attributes + effective state (resolved with provenance) + authorization. Single source of truth; a diagram never mutates it.
- Projection plane (view): Diagram document = Projection References (resource ID + presentation state) + Intent Preset + layer toggles + layout coordinates + Documentation Pins + migration journal + schema version. Projections are references, never duplicates.
- Metadata plane (rules): versioned resource-type metadata produced by provider adapters and governance-reviewed third-party metadata; resolves a record to a Presentation Role and Presentation Class; drives catalog, verbs, validation, effective-state computation, and honest fallbacks.

## 3. Presentation taxonomy
Roles (11): topology_node, container, attachment, selector_policy, inherited_policy, relationship, child_config, operational_artifact, metadata, ephemeral, unknown.
Classes (7): node, boundary, badge, overlay, edge, inspector_only, inventory_only.
Default role-to-class mapping: topology_node->node; container->boundary; attachment->badge; selector_policy->badge plus overlay in policy layer; inherited_policy->overlay with provenance; relationship->edge; child_config->inspector_only; operational_artifact->inspector_only (node only if metadata grants an intent-specific role); metadata->inspector_only; ephemeral->overlay in ephemeral layer only; unknown->inventory_only.

## 4. Deterministic classification decision tree
1) Validated metadata exists for (provider, type)? No -> role unknown, class inventory_only, placement blocked, banner 'unclassified/unsupported/needs classification' with optional request-classification action; never rendered as an ordinary node, never dropped. 2) Read role from type metadata; apply only metadata-authorized instance overrides (documentation pin, confirmed role override with journal entry). 3) Map role to class. 4) Apply intent preset, then layer toggles, then pins (fixed resolution order: truth -> type metadata -> instance override -> intent -> layer -> pin). 5) Compute effective state via adapter expansion (inheritance, selectors, attachments, hierarchy); if provider unverified or offline, mark derived state stale/last-known. 6) Validate relationships before any edge; never invent topology from names or icons; no arbitrary link or placement when semantics are unknown.

## 5. Default intent, views, and visibility rules
Default intent: Runtime topology - shows topology nodes, containers, typed relationships, and attachment badges on valid targets; hides child_config, metadata, operational_artifact, and standalone selector_policy/inherited_policy objects. Optional layers: Network, Security/Policy, Governance, Operations, Ephemeral; each reveals only its role set (the Security layer reveals non-routing association relationships). Visibility per (intent, layer, role, instance pin) with the fixed resolution order above. Intent switching never changes resource truth and never duplicates resources; a resource appears at most once per view. Content hidden by a switch is listed in the outline with per-layer counts and locate affordances; unsaved layout for now-hidden projections is stashed with a warning before the switch applies.

## 6. UI behaviors
- Catalog/palette: generated from registry; each entry displays the verb matching its role: Place (topology_node), Add child (container), Attach (attachment -> typed-target picker), Assign (selector_policy -> target/scope picker), Configure or Inspect (inspector_only), Pin for documentation (any resource via search/inventory). No universal 'click to add, drag to position'.
- Inventory: full authoritative resource list with search and filters (provider, role, hidden-from-diagram, unclassified, imported); actions: locate, inspect, pin, attach/assign.
- Outline/layers: visible projections plus per-layer hidden summaries with counts and locate links.
- Inspector: record truth, effective state with provenance breadcrumbs, valid target types and cardinality, invalid-relationship diagnostics, locate and show-in-inventory actions.
- Add/create: topology and container types added through the palette; attach/assign/configure/inspect flow through pickers and inspector; drag-position allowed only for node and boundary classes; badge/overlay positions are derived, not arbitrary.
- Pin: explicit documentation override; distinct visual style plus label; no ports; cannot receive edges except explicitly metadata-typed documentation links; flag 'runtime topology participant: false' so a pinned certificate/secret/tag/role assignment can never masquerade as runtime topology.

## 7. Registry/adapter contract (provider-neutral)
Per type: typeKey, displayName, provider, role, class, targetTypes, cardinality, scope, inheritance, selectors, effectiveStateHook, validationRules, fallbackRole, intentRoles (intent -> role), version, provenance, requiresConfirmation. Provider adapters map provider IDs and semantics into this contract and resolve effective state. The UI uses generic renderers per class plus registry metadata, never hard-coded type-specific components. Save documents record diagram schema version and registry version. Metadata changes are versioned, governed, and deprecatable; classification belongs primarily to type metadata with narrowly scoped instance overrides.

## 8. Category treatments
Known: per metadata. Unknown: inventory-only + banner + request-classification; placement and edges blocked. Unsupported/expired metadata: same honest fallback with the reason shown. Imported: identity-based migration; unrecognized -> unknown bucket + review list; never auto-classified by name or icon. Child: nested under parent record; child_config never a standalone node unless metadata says topology. Ephemeral: ephemeral layer only; no layout persistence; flagged transient. Attachment: badge on every valid target; shared attachment shows badge with count and expandable list; no duplicate records. Selector_policy: policy-layer badge/overlay; targets resolved by selectors; K8s NetworkPolicy selection live-updates with stale marker offline; multiple overlapping policies allowed. Inherited_policy: overlay with provenance breadcrumb; per-scope toggle; not duplicated per child. Operational_artifact: hidden by default; node only where metadata grants an operations-intent role; single renderer per view. Metadata (tags, locks, secrets, certificates, role assignments): inspector-only; pin allowed only as documentation pin.

## 9. Representative examples
- Azure VM with disk, NIC, IP config, NSG, backup, diagnostics, tags, locks, RBAC, alerts, snapshots: VM is a node; disks/NIC/IP config/snapshots/backup/diagnostics live in inspector or Operations layer; NSG appears as badge(s) on NIC/Subnet per the prior unanimous ruling (shared policy-library entry, typed target badges, no generic ports, no peer card); RBAC/tags/locks in Governance/Security layer plus inspector; no fake ports; no silent NIC treatment.
- AWS Security Group attached to ENI, Network ACL to Subnet, WAF Web ACL to protected resource, IAM policies to identities: attached/selector resources render as badges with counts; policy-layer reveal.
- GCP firewall rule targeting tags/service accounts: Security-layer selector badge with effective target list; hierarchical firewall and organization policies as inherited overlays with provenance; Cloud Armor as badge on backend services.
- Microsoft 365 Conditional Access/Intune/DLP/retention: inventory plus policy-layer overlay targeting users/groups/apps/devices/locations/sites; counts, never thousands of canvas edges; never topology nodes.
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy: network-layer overlay; Pod selection resolved live, stale marker offline; multiple policies listed distinctly.
- Centralized logging or security service: metadata declares intentRoles (operational_artifact in Runtime, topology_node in Operations), truthful in each view and never both in one view.
- Unknown newly released type and third-party/custom type: both land in the unknown inventory bucket with honest banner; no node until governed metadata exists.
- Imported all-cards diagram: migration reclassifies; valid topology becomes projections; NSG/policy cards become badges/overlays; unrecognized cards go to review; connections preserved only for validated topology relationships; everything else in 'needs review', never guessed.
- Documentation request for hidden certificate/secret/tag/role assignment: explicit documentation pin with distinct style, no ports or edges, labeled as documentation.

## 10. Validation, failure paths, rollback, stop conditions, testing/metrics, accessibility, compatibility
- Validation: registry schema and save-doc schema; target-type/cardinality/relationship validation; container cycle detection; effective-state checks; invalid relationships listed as diagnostics, never auto-fixed. Human/provider confirmation is required wherever semantics are ambiguous (new adapters, ambiguous migration, custom types).
- Failure paths: metadata missing -> unknown fallback; offline/unverified -> stale marker and placement blocked for unclassified types; effective-resolution failure -> last-known state plus banner; intent switch with unsaved layout -> stash and confirm; export always works and marks unknowns.
- Rollback: diagram snapshots plus migration journal with one-click revert; registry metadata version rollback with compatibility window; rollback never touches provider resources.
- Stop conditions: a type is placeable only with validated metadata and passing fixture tests; prototype exit requires a known-type set plus demonstrated honest fallback; rollout blocked unless rollback dry-run and accessibility gates pass; no new renderer while effective-state correctness gaps remain.
- Testing/metrics: golden-diagram fixtures per provider; taxonomy unit tests; migration fixtures including all-cards import and NSG reuse; accessibility automated plus manual; metrics: time-to-find hidden resource, misclassification rate, unknown-type rate, pin misuse (edges/ports attempted on pins), effective-state accuracy, verb misuse. Every destination adversarial scenario maps to a fixture or regression test.
- Accessibility: command palette and menus give non-drag alternatives for place/attach/assign/pin; keyboard-only flows; screen readers announce label, role, and visibility rationale (e.g., 'badge: NSG attached to NIC'); color-independent encoding (icon plus shape plus text); stable focus; zoom and density modes (collapse containers, cluster badges); WCAG 2.1 AA.
- Compatibility/migration: save-doc schema versioning and migration journal; the prior NSG treatment is preserved exactly; no resource loss (unknowns remain in inventory/review); no connection guessing; no irreversible provider changes; layout preserved where projections still exist.

## 11. Small textual product wireframe
Left panel: Catalog tab (grouped by class; per-item verb) + Inventory tab (search, filters, actions). Center: canvas; scene toolbar with Intent selector (Runtime, Network, Security, Governance, Operations, Ephemeral) and layer chips; topology nodes and boundaries; attachment badges under targets; documentation pins with distinct dashed outline and label; outline drawer with hidden-by-layer counts. Right panel: Inspector tabs: Record (truth + provenance), Effective (badges/inherited/selectors with breadcrumbs), Diagnostics (invalid relationships, unknowns); actions: Locate, Pin, Attach/Assign, Show in Inventory. Global command palette for all verbs (keyboard accessible).

## 14. Option ledger
| Option | Decision | Rationale |
| A (every resource as node) | Pruned as default; retained only as optional full-inventory list surface | Inventory dump, false topology, invalid ports, unusable density; controlled all-inventory list still has utility |
| B (provider-curated allowlist) | Pruned as whole architecture; retained as generated registry-derived placement defaults | Constant maintenance and one global answer ignore intent; generated near-allowlist is useful |
| C (universal taxonomy + automatic presentation) | Retained as core contract combined with adapters and fallbacks | Consistent, scalable, testable; wrong-classification risk mitigated by validated metadata, instance overrides, and honest unknown fallback |
| D (diagram-purpose presets/layers only) | Retained as projection mechanism; pruned as sole solution | Without taxonomy, presets become hard-coded filters that hide unpredictably; now metadata-driven |
| E (separate resource inventory from canvas) | Retained | Completeness and discoverability; shared identity plus locate links prevent duplicate truth |
| F (user visibility/pinning as primary rule) | Pruned as primary; retained as explicit pin override only | Pushes domain modeling onto users; pins safe only within documented constraints |
| G (hybrid registry + intent projections) | Selected | Correctness, scalability, context, discoverability, and user control; resolution order, fallbacks, catalog behavior, persistence boundary, and testing are concrete |

## 15. Scope exclusions and retained unknowns
No code; no exhaustive classification of every provider type; no policy/IAM/monitoring/cost/compliance editors; no final icons/colors/typography/spacing or design tokens; no provider APIs/permissions/deployment beyond the UI/data contract; the full inventory is never the default architecture diagram. Retained unknowns: exhaustive per-type classification (out of scope by decision), provider API details, design tokens, staffing/owners, and exact legacy saved-diagram format details (verified during WP09).

vote.summary: v0 is a decision request, not an artifact. Proposed Option G hybrid: authoritative registry/inventory + deterministic presentation taxonomy + intent-based diagram projections. All 13 acceptance criteria, all options A-G, the prior NSG ruling, and all required adversarial scenarios are covered; deferred items are explicit work packages with gates; no blocking objections; confidence high.
